name: Primary Unilateral Adrenal Hyperplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Unilateral Adrenal Hyperplasia

criteria.description: Imaging evidence of unilateral adrenal gland enlargement or nodularity
Elevated adrenal hormone levels consistent with hyperplasia (e.g., cortisol, aldosterone) without contralateral adrenal involvement
Exclusion of adrenal adenoma or pheochromocytoma by imaging and biochemical testing
Histopathological confirmation of adrenal hyperplasia if adrenalectomy performed
Presence of clinical signs consistent with adrenal hormone excess (e.g., hypertension, hypokalemia)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral adrenal enlargement on imaging plus biochemical evidence of adrenal hormone excess with exclusion of adrenal adenoma and pheochromocytoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, radiology, and pathology.

laboratory: Elevated plasma aldosterone concentration with suppressed plasma renin activity
Elevated serum cortisol levels with abnormal dexamethasone suppression test
imaging: CT or MRI showing unilateral adrenal gland enlargement or nodularity
Absence of adrenal adenoma or pheochromocytoma features on imaging
genetic: Somatic mutations in genes regulating adrenal growth and steroidogenesis (e.g., KCNJ5 mutations in some cases)
other: Histopathology showing adrenal cortical hyperplasia without adenoma formation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of discrete adrenal mass on imaging
Histopathology confirming adenoma rather than hyperplasia
Typically unilateral but with different biochemical profile
Elevated catecholamines or metanephrines in plasma or urine
Imaging showing adrenal mass with characteristic features
Symptoms of episodic hypertension, palpitations, and sweating
Bilateral adrenal gland enlargement on imaging
Different hormonal profile often involving cortisol or androgen excess
May present with congenital adrenal hyperplasia features

redFlags: Rapid onset of adrenal mass with systemic symptoms
